sources.title: Deepwater Physical Oceanography Reanalysis and Synthesis of Historical Data: Synthesis Report
Gulf of Mexico Physical Oceanography Program, Final Report: Year 3, Volume II: Technical Report

decisions.locator: Table A-1, 1984 Loop Current Eddy separations
decisions.finding: The source explicitly identifies Slim Chance as an alias of Eddy Arnold.
decisions.date_conflict: Source lists August 1984; the registry lists initial separation on 1984-09-16. Neither date is overwritten.
decisions.decision: Retain as an alias research lead. No dimensions, whole lifetime, physical identity crosswalk, or registry alias installed.

decisions.finding: The approximately 330 km drifter loops occur in July-August 1986 after possible coalescence of B and C.
decisions.decision: Exclude as an individual Hot Core dimension.

decisions.finding: The 80 km radius and 75 cm/s swirl speed refer to Eddy B in mid-February 1986.
decisions.decision: Do not transfer these measurements to Eddy C.

decisions.finding: The approximately 200 km diameter refers to companion cyclone Eddy Z.
decisions.decision: Exclude as a Hot Core measurement; this page was checked as text only in this review.

decisions.finding: The western warm zone has no identified southern boundary and does not specifically delineate the embedded eddies.
decisions.decision: Do not derive a full eddy width from the warm-zone latitude extent.

decisions.finding: An approximately 450 km hydrographic diameter is described for an unnamed feature surveyed in May 1987.
decisions.decision: Retain unassigned. A nearby year or registry separation date does not establish its name.

decisions.finding: Drifter 3379 has separate March and April 1986 track panels with daily markers. The plotted monthly envelopes combine orbital motion and translation.
decisions.decision: Potential trajectory digitization source only. No track-envelope width is admitted as a closed eddy boundary or diameter. Caption dates begin March 8; placement in prose is March 7.

date_cautions: SAIC describes Eddy C separation as January 1986 in some passages and February 1986 on PDF page 84; its registry initial-separation date is 1985-11-08. These are unresolved event definitions, not an inferred lifetime.
The source synthesis associates Hot Eddy with Eddy C and separately lists Hot Core in January 1986. This context is insufficient to transfer unrelated B, Z, or merged B/C measurements.
next_source_targets: Transcribe the verified Fast/Eddy B hydrographic area table into qualified thermal-level size references, keeping each survey and temperature-surface depth contour distinct; zero and unclosed levels require explicit handling.
Locate the original 1984 Slim Chance/Arnold survey or operational chart using the explicit alias, with dimensions or a dated traceable boundary.
Seek unmerged Eddy C hydrography or an explicit orbital radius before the possible B/C coalescence; preserve orbit versus outer-boundary semantics.
Resolve the name of the May 1987 surveyed anticyclone from a primary alias or explicit trajectory chronology before assigning its reported 450 km scale.

execution.reason: Evidence review only; no source register, builder, browser, runtime, or release behavior changed.

verified_numeric_source_lead.alias_status: Existing explicit B/Fast alias; preserve the already qualified date and identity association.
verified_numeric_source_lead.quantity: Area enclosed by a specified depth contour of the 8 degree Celsius temperature surface
cautions: Depth headers label the depth of the 8 degree Celsius temperature surface, not a measured whole-eddy thickness or sampling depth.
Different depth contours are nested thermal-level areas, not interchangeable full outer-boundary areas or principal widths.
The November 750 m cell is printed as zero. Do not interpret it as disappearance of Eddy B or silently convert it into missing data.
The January and April 550 m cells are printed as dashes; accompanying prose says contours shallower than 600 m no longer closed around the eddy. Do not fill them with zero or interpolate.
Monthly survey rows do not establish an annual envelope or complete lifetime; some surveys span multiple weeks.
